name: Peak Hour Payment Switch
tagline: Keep a peak-hour switch stable under load.
narrative:
It is Friday afternoon. YamusaPay is processing a sustained mix of consumer transfers, international payments, and urgent payroll.

The low-cost provider becomes slow and unreliable, while another provider has a short outage. Every accepted payment remains in flight, so routing decisions change future queue pressure and capacity.
objective: Maximise completed payments while limiting timeouts, priority misses, overload rejections, failures, queue growth, and operating score.
learningObjective: Design an adaptive policy that accounts for the future effect of each routing decision.
intelligenceExplanation:
The starting brain is empty. Your policy must distinguish flexible low-value work from urgent, high-value, payroll, and international payments.

Holding can protect a provider during a short incident, but holding everything causes deadlines to expire. A fixed provider choice fails when the incident schedule changes.
hint: Treat `deadlineRemaining` and `capacityRemaining` as scarce resources. Route urgent work to an eligible healthy provider; use cost and congestion for flexible work.
hints: Create early branches for near-deadline, priority, payroll, and high-value traffic.
For flexible traffic, compare eligible routes using expected cost, health score, current latency, and remaining capacity.
After a failed attempt, prefer an eligible provider other than lastProviderA/B/C; retry only while deadline budget remains.
brief: Adapt routing as queues, latency, capacity, and traffic priority change.
context: Provider latency grows with load, capacity is finite, retries consume time, and deadlines continue counting down.

steps.label: Segment traffic by urgency, value, and transaction type
Route using live capacity, congestion, latency, reliability, and cost
Handle retryable failures without repeating a broken route
Finish the visible surge with at most two timeouts
Submit the unchanged policy against the peak-hour hidden suite

objectives.label: Allow no more than two timeouts
Allow no more than one urgent-payment failure
Keep the visible penalty score below 100

rubric: Outage, recovery, capacity, and retry correctness: 25%

goals.description: Keep mixed payment traffic flowing safely under peak load.

states.description: Evaluate the live switch once per decision tick.

functions.description: Attempt the current payment through Provider A.
Attempt the current payment through Provider B.
Attempt the current payment through Provider C.
Wait one tick while provider work and deadlines advance.
